title: Narrow @override dead-code suppression to framework callbacks
description:
Codex review finding from sutra/111. Currently every `@override` method sets FLAG_FFI_ENTRY (0x04), which suppresses it from dead-code analysis via `(s.flags & 7) = 0`. In Dart, `@override` is ubiquitous for any interface/superclass contract — this hides genuinely dead overridden methods in project-internal hierarchies.

The original intent was to prevent false positives for Flutter lifecycle methods (build, initState, dispose) that are called by the framework, not by indexed code. But the blanket @override approach is too broad.

Options:
1. Only suppress for known Flutter lifecycle method names (build, initState, dispose, didChangeDependencies, etc.) with @override
2. Introduce a separate FLAG_OVERRIDE bit (0x08) that dead-code analysis can treat differently from FLAG_FFI_ENTRY — e.g., only suppress overrides in classes extending framework base classes
3. Don't flag @override at all; instead add framework superclass detection (extends State, StatelessWidget, etc.) and flag the whole class
4. Keep current behavior but document the trade-off — broader suppression prevents false positives at the cost of missing some dead overrides"

acceptance_criteria.text: @override methods whose name is NOT in the Dart lifecycle allowlist are no longer suppressed from sutra_dead results
Known lifecycle methods (build, initState, dispose, didChangeDependencies, didUpdateWidget, deactivate, reassemble) with @override still suppressed from dead-code
A new FLAG_OVERRIDE (0x08) bit is set on all @override methods, not included in the dead-code suppression mask
The lifecycle method list is shared between dart.rs and trace.rs (single source of truth)
Existing tests pass; new test covers the narrowed suppression behavior

implementation_plan:
# Implementation Plan

## Approach

Split the current blanket `@override → FLAG_FFI_ENTRY` into two concerns: (1) a new informational `FLAG_OVERRIDE` (0x08) set on all `@override` methods, and (2) `FLAG_FFI_ENTRY` set only when the overriding method name is in a shared Dart lifecycle allowlist. The dead-code mask `(s.flags & 7) = 0` stays unchanged — bit 0x08 passes through, so non-lifecycle overrides become visible to `sutra_dead`. The lifecycle list already exists in `trace.rs`; extract it to `dart.rs` as a `pub const` and reuse from both sites.

## Files

- **Modify**: `src/parser/rust.rs` (line 41) — add `FLAG_OVERRIDE = 0x08`
- **Modify**: `src/parser/dart.rs` (lines 3, 533–562) — add shared lifecycle const, narrow the `@override` flag logic, pass short_name into `extract_flags`
- **Modify**: `src/tools/trace.rs` (lines 25–34, 279) — import and reuse the shared lifecycle list from `dart.rs`
- **Test**: `src/parser/dart.rs` (existing test module) — add test for narrowed override behavior

## Steps

### Step 1: Add FLAG_OVERRIDE constant

In `src/parser/rust.rs`, add the new flag constant alongside the existing ones:

```rust
pub const FLAG_TEST: u32 = 0x01;
pub const FLAG_CFG_TEST: u32 = 0x02;
pub const FLAG_FFI_ENTRY: u32 = 0x04;
pub const FLAG_OVERRIDE: u32 = 0x08;
```

No other changes in this file. The dead-code query mask `& 7` already excludes bit 0x08.

### Step 2: Add shared lifecycle constant and narrow extract_flags in dart.rs

Add a `pub const` lifecycle array in `dart.rs`:

```rust
pub const DART_LIFECYCLE_METHODS: &[&str] = &[
    "build", "initState", "dispose",
    "didChangeDependencies", "didUpdateWidget",
    "deactivate", "reassemble",
];
```

Update the import line to also bring in `FLAG_OVERRIDE`:

```rust
use crate::parser::rust::{FLAG_CFG_TEST, FLAG_FFI_ENTRY, FLAG_OVERRIDE, FLAG_TEST};
```

Change `extract_flags` signature to accept the short name:

```rust
fn extract_flags(node: Node, src: &[u8], file_path: &str, short_name: Option<&str>) -> u32 {
```

Replace the override block (lines 547–549):

```rust
if has_annotation(node, src, "override") {
    flags |= FLAG_OVERRIDE;
    if short_name.is_some_and(|n| DART_LIFECYCLE_METHODS.contains(&n)) {
        flags |= FLAG_FFI_ENTRY;
    }
}
```

### Step 3: Update all extract_flags call sites in dart.rs

There are ~13 call sites. Methods/functions have `sym.short_name` available; classes/enums/type_aliases pass `None`:

- Lines 56, 73, 88, 103: class/mixin/extension/enum declarations → `extract_flags(child, src, file_path, None)`
- Lines 116, 131, 161, 179, 185: method/function/declaration/constructor → `extract_flags(child, src, file_path, Some(&sym.short_name))`
- Lines 366, 387, 411: nested method extraction sites → `extract_flags(node, src, file_path, Some(&sym.short_name))`

### Step 4: Refactor trace.rs to reuse shared list

In `src/tools/trace.rs`, import the shared constant:

```rust
use crate::parser::dart::DART_LIFECYCLE_METHODS;
```

Rewrite `is_known_entry_point`:

```rust
pub fn is_known_entry_point(short_name: &str, kind: &str) -> bool {
    match short_name {
        "main" => true,
        name if kind == "method" => DART_LIFECYCLE_METHODS.contains(&name),
        _ => false,
    }
}
```

Update `entry_point_rules_doc` (line 279) to reference the constant instead of a hardcoded list:

```rust
"dart": std::iter::once("main")
    .chain(DART_LIFECYCLE_METHODS.iter().copied())
    .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
```

### Step 5: Add tests

Add a test in `dart.rs` test module that parses a Dart snippet with:
- `@override void build(...)` → has both `FLAG_OVERRIDE` and `FLAG_FFI_ENTRY`
- `@override void fetchItems(...)` → has `FLAG_OVERRIDE` only, NOT `FLAG_FFI_ENTRY`
- `@pragma('vm:entry-point') void main(...)` → has `FLAG_FFI_ENTRY` only

Verify the first two via `sym.flags & FLAG_FFI_ENTRY` and `sym.flags & FLAG_OVERRIDE` assertions.

## Acceptance criteria coverage

- [x] "Non-lifecycle @override methods visible to sutra_dead" → Steps 2–3 (narrowed flag logic)
- [x] "Lifecycle methods still suppressed" → Step 2 (allowlist check before FLAG_FFI_ENTRY)
- [x] "@pragma('vm:entry-point') still suppresses" → Step 2 (pragma block unchanged)
- [x] "FLAG_OVERRIDE (0x08) set on all overrides" → Steps 1–2
- [x] "Shared lifecycle list" → Steps 2, 4
- [x] "Tests" → Step 5

messages.text: Codex review: needs-attention. One medium finding — variable extraction branches (lines 376-421) pass Some(&sym.short_name) to extract_flags, so an @override field named 'build' or 'dispose' would get FLAG_FFI_ENTRY and be hidden from dead-code. Should pass None for variable/field call sites since fields can't be lifecycle callbacks.
